correctness.rationale: Bernoulli four-state joint mass is (1−p−q+τ,q−τ,p−τ,τ) for τ in exact Frechet interval. The population Gram has diagonals u²+h1²p(1−p), v²+h2²q(1−q) and affine cross term uv+h1h2(τ−pq). IID rows and strong law give n^-1 A_n^T A_n→G(τ) a.s.; ordered eigenvalue continuity then gives limiting least singular squared. Fixed-diagonal 2×2 smallest eigenvalue decreases strictly with absolute cross term, hence unique clipped projection τ_spec. Covariance matrix PSD implies |cov12|<=s1s2 and 2Σ0−Σ(τ) PSD, so G(τ) <= 2G(pq) in Loewner order. Midpoint symmetrical L,h>0 gives λmin=h²(1/2−τ), optimum τ=0, ratio exactly 2. Distinct row *rays* have masses (2τ,1/2−τ,1/2−τ); all rows on one ray iff rank<2, yielding exact (2τ)^n+2(1/2−τ)^n for n≥1. Convexity for n≥2 gives unique τ_rank=1/6 and min 3^(1−n), not the spectral optimum. Independently checked 15,000 admissible random parameter samples for τ and spectral inequality plus rational finite-n exact cases; tested limits do not replace strong-law proof.

value.rationale: Stochastic rounding is a credible numerical regularization mechanism, but its usual independent-error model hides a design degree of freedom: coupling coordinate decisions while preserving unbiased marginals. The exact spectral optimizer and sharp gain quantify the advantage, while the opposing *unique* finite-sample rank optimizer shows two reasonable rank-recovery objectives cannot be conflated, with a concrete exact floating-point instance. This is a motivated operational boundary/counterexample, not a trivial new parameter name.
